CN: Factory orders and production

The June official manufacturing PMI edged up to 49.0 from 48.8. The distinction inside the survey is more informative than the change in the headline. Production crossed into expansion, while new orders remained below the 50-point dividing line. A factory can restart a production line to complete existing orders without receiving enough new work to keep that line busy next month. China’s statistics bureau reported steadier conditions in automobiles, rail and shipping equipment, and electrical machinery. A recovery thesis that depends on export or domestic orders catching up with output therefore needs confirmation beyond the better headline. [ec03nf]
Credit transmission

The one-year loan prime rate fell to 3.55% on June 20 and the over-five-year rate, used as a mortgage reference, to 4.20%. Lower borrowing rates can benefit a viable project waiting on financing. A company whose customers are still drawing down stock has less reason to expand capacity just because a loan is a little cheaper. The official survey showed large enterprises back above 50 while the small-firm reading slipped further into contraction. Favour evidence of actual orders or improved financing access at smaller suppliers before treating cheaper benchmark credit as an across-the-board industrial recovery. [ec03lr] [ec03nf]
PL: Household purchasing power

Statistics Poland’s flash June reading put consumer inflation at 11.5% year on year, with prices unchanged from May. That combination matters for Polish consumer businesses. A household can see its monthly bill stop rising and still face a substantially higher cost of living than a year earlier. For a grocery chain, nominal revenue can continue rising while customers buy fewer items or choose cheaper products. The better evidence of a genuine consumer recovery would be improvement in volumes and in spending beyond essentials. A single unchanged monthly index gives little basis for assuming that adjustment has already happened. [ec03fl]
First-home mortgage channel

The government’s subsidised first-home mortgage program is scheduled to begin accepting applications at participating banks on July 3. Seven banks said they were ready for the first day, including PKO Bank Polski and Bank Pekao. The ministry sets a PLN 500,000 loan ceiling for an individual and PLN 600,000 for specified family households, with ten years of instalment support. The first observable change should be in enquiries and applications. It will take longer to learn whether banks approve those applicants, households find eligible properties and developers convert interest into sales. [ec03ms]

CN: Domestic orders and exporters

Caixin’s manufacturing PMI came in at 50.5 in June, down from 50.9. Its manufacturers reported a modest increase in overall orders and broadly unchanged new export business. Place that beside the official PMI of 49.0. The different survey panels give a picture of uneven activity around the expansion threshold. The Caixin report is particularly useful for understanding the source of what growth there was. A domestic customer taking delivery can keep a line running now; it tells a component producer much less about when overseas clients will be ready to rebuild their inventories. [ec04cp] [ec04nf]
Pricing and working capital

Input costs and selling prices fell in the Caixin survey. A fall in both can improve or damage a manufacturer’s margins, depending on how quickly it reprices finished goods and what it paid for inventory already in the warehouse. A firm buying inputs at today’s lower cost and holding its output price has a different outlook from one discounting older goods to keep orders flowing. In an earnings review, put inventory turnover and collection of trade receivables alongside reported revenue growth. The next strong signal would be rising orders without a further sacrifice on selling prices. [ec04cp]
PL: Factories and backlogs

Poland’s manufacturing PMI dropped from 47.0 to 45.1 points in June. PKO Bank Polski reported pronounced declines in new orders and production and a thirteenth consecutive monthly reduction in outstanding work. A factory can use its backlog to keep skilled staff employed through a bad month. As that backlog gets smaller, today’s missing order becomes a more immediate threat to hours worked and the next shift. Inputs arriving sooner can look like better operating performance even when the buyer simply has fewer orders to place. Check whether new work is stabilising before treating faster delivery or lower costs as evidence of recovery. [ec04pp]
Two domestic demand cycles

The opening of first-home mortgage applications makes domestic property a poor proxy for the factory cycle this week. A subsidised instalment can improve affordability for an eligible borrower while leaving an export manufacturer’s financing cost or order book untouched. The benefit to a bank arrives in stages: application, underwriting, approval and disbursement. A developer can benefit from a reservation before it recognises revenue. These lags matter if a front-page rush to submit paperwork lifts shares across both banking and construction. Compare conversion to completed transactions before extrapolating from the first stage into earnings. [ec04ms] [ec04pp]

CN: Export permits in the production schedule

China’s new licensing requirements for certain gallium and germanium products are due to start August 1. AXT said its Chinese manufacturing business would seek permits to continue shipping affected semiconductor substrates. The operating risk is visible before any change in the price of the materials. A supplier may need to assemble end-user information and decide which orders can ship on the promised schedule. A customer may arrange a second supplier or hold extra stocks in case approval takes longer than planned. Each response can tie up cash even if every application is eventually approved. [ec05cnm] [ec05ax]
Reading component orders

The June Caixin factory survey found export orders broadly unchanged and the expansion in output slowing. Against that backdrop, a sudden rise in requests for an affected substrate could reflect precautionary buying rather than stronger final demand for electronics. Check whether deliveries and repeat orders hold up after customers have accumulated a buffer. A pause at a licensing desk can push one company’s sale from one quarter to the next without changing the final user’s appetite. The strongest industrial evidence would be broader and more durable: rising new orders across unaffected products alongside reliable delivery schedules for the affected ones. [ec05cp] [ec05ax]
PL: Pricing power along the factory chain

PKO Bank Polski’s reading of the manufacturing survey highlights rapid declines in both purchasing costs and the prices manufacturers charge customers. A supplier to an export-oriented plant may secure cheaper materials and still lose margin if its customer demands the saving immediately. Fixed costs become a further burden if the plant operates fewer shifts. For investors assessing a manufacturer’s results, changes in gross margin and physical volume together are more revealing than a decline in its energy or materials bill. An improved margin on fewer units need not restore the level of operating profit. [ec05pp]
Where falling inflation can help first

The flash consumer index was flat month on month in June but 11.5% above its year-earlier level. For a Polish household with room to postpone purchases, stable shop prices make it easier to plan. That benefit works through disposable income more slowly than a visible monthly move in fuel or food. It is also distinct from the government’s support for first-home borrowers, which is confined to eligibility rules and a capped mortgage amount. A business relying on broader consumption should look for improving sales volumes outside housing and essential goods before committing to a larger order book. [ec05fl] [ec05ms]

CN: Services after reopening

Caixin’s June services business activity index fell to 53.9, still in expansion but at the weakest pace since the recovery began in January. New business grew more slowly while staffing increased and confidence about the year ahead improved. For a hotel or travel operator this is a recognisable combination: staff can be recruited to meet a higher level of bookings even as the monthly increase in bookings begins to slow. The distinction matters to valuations built on another acceleration. Watch the pace at which new business arrives alongside bookings already on hand before assuming that adding staff will lift margins. [ec06sv]
Which businesses can pass costs through?

The service-company survey found rising input costs and only a slight increase in selling prices. The factory survey showed purchasing costs and output charges falling. This is an operating difference between the two sides of reopening. A manufacturer may benefit from buying a commodity more cheaply while a service company has to pay more to attract staff. Neither can count on passing through costs when demand is unremarkable. Prefer businesses able to increase the number of paying customers without increasing expenses in proportion. A stronger composite index by itself is insufficient evidence that either sector has regained pricing power. [ec06sv] [ec06cp]
PL: The rate decision still ahead

The reference rate entering the July meeting is 6.75% under the June Monetary Policy Council decision. The June flash inflation reading of 11.5% and the weaker factory survey offer policymakers a reason to consider how far tightening has already travelled. They leave a less straightforward question about the pace of any eventual easing. A household deciding whether to start a mortgage weighs its current monthly payment; a manufacturer signing a long supply contract weighs the future cost of carrying stocks and collecting receivables. Monetary restraint can show up in those decisions at quite different times. [ec06june] [ec06fl] [ec06pp]
Banks versus loan applicants

The subsidised first-home scheme changes the cost of an eligible mortgage without changing the rate businesses pay to fund their inventory. The largest banks participating in the program may receive a larger pipeline of enquiries even if credits outside the program remain weak. For bank earnings, the useful follow-up is the number of approved applications that become disbursed loans, together with funding costs and credit risk. For builders, reservations need to turn into contracts and eventual handovers. Keep these channels separate when comparing a rally in lenders with continued weakness among manufacturers reporting fewer new orders. [ec06ms] [ec06pp]

CN: Borrowers and bank margins

June’s cuts in both the one-year and longer loan prime rates can matter in different places on a company’s accounts. Cheaper short-term borrowing eases the cost of carrying raw materials for an established operating business. A lower long-term mortgage benchmark can improve the affordability calculation for a household thinking of buying a home. Neither borrower has to take up the offer. A factory with excess stock can repay working capital instead of expanding production, while a household unsure about future income can defer a purchase. Compare actual lending and customer orders before inferring more revenue for lenders or industrial suppliers. [ec07lr] [ec07cp]
Service exports and staffing

Travel and tourism supported overseas orders at the service companies surveyed by Caixin. The same release reports solid growth in input prices and only a small rise in the prices charged to customers. A hotel selling an extra room or a travel agency accepting another reservation may be able to use capacity it already has; a business that needs to hire extra people faces a different cost. Look for the combination of overseas demand, repeat domestic bookings and sustainable staffing expenses. That tells more about the durability of a service recovery than a return to normal tourist activity at one destination. [ec07sv]
PL: Borrowing before the subsidy

BIK’s June housing data add a useful check on the emerging mortgage narrative. The value of lender enquiries per working day rose 26.5% from June 2022; 22,010 potential borrowers applied, up 12.8% year on year, while the applicant count fell 1.6% from May. The average loan requested rose to PLN 382,060. Those figures precede the July launch of subsidised first-home mortgages. They give investors a baseline against which to judge the launch, with two important qualifications: the earlier year provides a weak base, and enquiries have yet to become approved or disbursed credit. [ec07bi]
What the Council held fixed

The Council kept the reference rate at 6.75%. It put the 2024 inflation range at 3.7%–6.8% with 50% probability, conditioned on unchanged NBP rates and information available through June 22. Read that range as an illustration of the risks policymakers face. It says little about the exact date of a first cut. An investor expecting a quick improvement in leveraged consumer businesses should require evidence of both easing inflation and credit actually reaching borrowers. Quoting the conditional projection as though it incorporates a sequence of promised rate cuts would count the policy benefit before it is delivered. [ec07nb]

CN: Foreign investment and supply decisions

US Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen’s Beijing visit brought direct discussions with American businesses and Chinese officials. In her concluding remarks she distinguished supply-chain diversification and targeted national-security measures from a broad separation of the economies. Improved communication can matter to an operating company that needs a timely answer about licenses, data rules or customer access. It reduces uncertainty about whom to ask. A board approving a long-lived plant still needs the actual terms, a reliable market for its output and some confidence that goods or services can move across the border after the investment is sunk. A diplomatic meeting alone supplies none of those contractual protections. [ec10us] [ec10us2]
Mapping the bottleneck

AXT’s decision to seek permits for exports from its Chinese manufacturing business illustrates the narrow question executives face. A semiconductor substrate can be made on schedule, at the expected cost, and still reach a foreign customer late. Work backwards from the required delivery date: qualification of an alternative supplier, the customer’s inventory buffer, application processing and the ability to finance stock during a delay all matter. A credible improvement would be a clear process with predictable outcomes. Until then a supplier with a diversified customer base and a buyer with more than one qualified source may have quite different exposures to the same rule. [ec10ax] [ec10cnm]
PL: Who benefited from the first leg of disinflation?

The Council said the June decline in annual inflation came chiefly from energy and, to a smaller extent, food and some other goods. It also noted annual declines in May retail sales, industrial output and construction output. A lower annual rate can relieve pressure on households before it rebuilds demand for discretionary purchases. For an industrial supplier, a lower energy cost improves the price it can quote, but weak factory volumes make fixed costs harder to absorb. The distinction supports a selective view of Polish equities rather than assuming the same inflation surprise lifts consumers, exporters and banks equally. [ec10nb] [ec10pp]
The mortgage funnel

June applicants requested an average PLN 382,060 according to BIK. Compare the number of people applying with the amount they request as the subsidised first-home program starts. Bigger average loans can lift the aggregate value of enquiries even if the applicant base changes little. The count is also a better first check on whether new people are entering the market, although it says nothing by itself about credit quality. A bank or developer trading on a surge in housing demand eventually needs approved financing and completed sales. Track these stages before treating a busy application system as an immediate improvement in earnings. [ec10bi] [ec10ms]

CN: Disinflation beneath the headline

China’s June CPI was unchanged from a year earlier. Food prices rose 2.3%, non-food prices fell 0.6%, and core CPI excluding food and energy rose 0.4%. The distinctions change the valuation read-through. A retailer selling fresh food faces a different set of price changes from a seller of durable goods. When aggregate prices are flat, reported sales can still be affected as households trade between products or as merchants offer promotions. Look for improving unit volumes alongside evidence that margins can hold. A rise in revenue concentrated in the categories where prices went up would be thin evidence of a general recovery in consumption. [ec11pc] [ec11pc2]
Industrial inputs and selling prices

Factory-gate prices fell 5.4% over the year and 0.8% from May. The statistics bureau also reported double-digit annual declines in manufacturers’ purchasing prices for chemical raw materials, ferrous metals and fuel and power. Those are potentially meaningful cost savings for downstream producers. They also represent weaker revenue for businesses selling the same inputs. The timing of inventory purchases can magnify the difference: a firm holding expensive earlier stock can suffer a margin squeeze in a market where replacement inputs are already cheaper. Assess where each company sits in the supply chain before treating producer deflation as a reason to buy or sell the whole industrial sector. [ec11ppi]
PL: The central forecast and the surrounding range

The July Inflation Report projects Polish GDP growth of 0.6% in 2023, 2.4% in 2024 and 3.3% in 2025. Its central inflation path is 11.9%, 5.2% and 3.6% respectively. These are annual averages in a conditional projection; they need not match a particular monthly reading. The projected combination leaves room for inflation to slow considerably while growth remains weak this year. A domestic consumer company may therefore report less pressure from input costs before any substantial improvement in demand. Consider its capacity to protect margins at lower volumes as carefully as its exposure to an eventual household recovery. [ec11inf] [ec11ir]
A specific credit test

The Council’s public projection conditions on unchanged policy rates. The new first-home mortgage program, meanwhile, can improve the affordability of qualifying home purchases without any change in the NBP rate. BIK’s June applicant count and average requested amount offer two ways to follow through on that distinction. Ask whether the new applications broaden the borrower base and whether approved loans actually finance transactions. A subsidised increase in housing credit can coexist with weak working-capital demand from factories. For a lender, a better mortgage pipeline and a recovering corporate loan book are separate earnings assumptions and should be valued separately. [ec11nb] [ec11bi] [ec11ms]
